newsitem.title: USA: Canmax sees 30-50 pct revenue growth in fiscal 97.
newsitem.headline: Canmax sees 30-50 pct revenue growth in fiscal 97.

text.p: Canmax Inc expects its revenues to grow 30-50 percent in fiscal 1997 and should run up profits of 15-20 cents after overcoming heavy losses in recent years, company executives said.

"It kind of depends on how a few things go, but we are very comfortable with 15-20 cents-plus earnings on a full year basis for fiscal 1997," Chief Financial Officer Philip Parsons said in an interview this week.
"We are positioned really well at the moment...We could see revenue growth in the 30-50 percent range for fiscal 1997 full year over fiscal 1996," he said.

The Irving, Texas-based company, a supplier of information and automation services to the retail petroleum and convenience store industry, on Thurday released its results for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 1996, which ended October 31.

It said fourth quarter earnings per share were six cents, compared to two cents in the same period last year and that earnings per share for fiscal 1996 were two cents compared with a loss of 79 cents in fiscal 1995.
Revenues for fiscal 1996 were $12.26 million, up from $9.00 million last year.
Parsons said Canmax made a loss of $3.7 million in fiscal year 1995 and lost $6.5 million the previous year.

Chief Executive Officer Roger Bryant said a restructuring program which began in 1994 had cut costs and left the company well placed to take advantage of an upturn in the industry after several difficult years.
"We got our own house in order and where we are today is not a function of the industry turnaround, but where we plan to go is certainly dependent on that," Bryant said.
Parsons said he expects revenues in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, which ends January 31, to be about 30 percent higher than in the same period of fiscal 1996, when they totalled $3.07 million.
He said first quarter earnings per share would likely be in the 3-5 cents range.
